newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak cbank says targets hold despite SKK attacks.
newsitem.headline: Slovak cbank says targets hold despite SKK attacks.

text.p: The National Bank of Slovakia (NBS) is not considering changing its 1997 monetary programme, and still considers its main targets achievable despite turbulence from a recent attack on the crown.

NBS Vice-governor Marian Jusko told Reuters on Monday that the recent wave of downward pressure on the crown was only a short-term phenomenon and unlikely to be repeated, making policy targets for the year still within reach.
"The recent month (on the foreign exchange) was just a short-term tremble and I believe that this phenomenon will not be repeated," Jusko said.

The NBS 1997 monetary programme sets an annual inflation target of 4.9-5.7 percent, with growth in the money supply, the central bank's main yardstick for assessing monetary development, targeted at a year-on-year rate of 10.7 percent.
The NBS has been battling downward pressure against the crown over the past month, sparked by speculative short- selling of crowns by foreign investors playing on the currency's perceived weakness.

The central bank has moved to choke liquidity on the local money market by limiting access to crowns while at the same time fixing the crown stronger against market levels to make speculation against the currency expensive.

The crown briefly touched the lower floor of its plus-minus seven percent mark/dollar fluctuation band, but has since stabilised between basket parity and -0.1 percent on the band's depreciation side over the past two weeks.
The NBS battle for currency stability has brought about an acute liquidity shortage on the money market and pushed interbank money rates above 30 percent.

"The (interbank) rates are not sustainable for the longer-term, but we will continue adding liquidity to the banking sector which should push rates to levels where they were before the attack on the currency," Jusko said.
Interbank rates traded below 20 percent just before the start of the run on the crown around one month ago.
Jusko would not elaborate when the NBS expected the rates to return to their previous levels.
